newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian life office makes strong market debut.
newsitem.headline: Australian life office makes strong market debut.

text.p: Australia's second largest life insurer, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, listed simultaneously on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges on Tuesday and immediately yielded a profit of almost 10 percent.
National Mutal shares opened at A$1.75 ($1.38), a 15 cent or 9.4 percent premium to the group's institutional subscription price of A$1.60 per share.
The A$1.50 issue price for individual shareholders, mostly National Mutual policyholders, offered an even larger premium of 25 cents a share or 16.6 percent.
The price set its market value at around A$3.0 billion.
The group's institutional share offer was oversubscribed six times and the final price of A$1.60 per share was higher than indicative bidding range of A$1.35 to A$1.55 initially set.

National Mutual is owned 51 percent by French insurance and financial services giant Axa SA, which is prevented under the terms of the float from selling down its stake for six months after the listing.
Axa effectively bought into National Mutual last year at around A$1.25 per share.

National Mutual's listing completes its 21-month transition from a mutual company owned by its policyholders to a listed group free to pursue its strategic focus on Asia, unshackled by a mutual requirement to act solely in policyholders' interests.
